free_tier.stated: Route64 provides IPv6 tunnels with a routed /56 subnet, delivered through multiple tunnel protocols (WireGuard, GRE, IP6IP, etc.) to your endpoint.

egress.terms: Traffic is not metered and it is possible to get more transit if 200M is not enough. (transit text) The IPv6 tunnelbroker page publishes no byte allowance at all; the conditions page says 'This is a free best effort service.'; ingress: tcp+udp

interface_detail: self-service web portal generates the tunnel configuration; wg-quick applies it
tooling: wg-quick plus the vendor portal; GRE/SIT/L2TPv3/VXLAN also offered
chaining: a routed /56 over WireGuard gives a free VM with no public address 2^72 inbound IPv6 addresses; the VM supplies the CPU and a user supplies only a WireGuard handshake

limits.value: designed for up to 200 Mbit/s; throttle at any time

binding_note: Nothing in the vocabulary fails at 1 TiB/month. There is no byte counter on the tunnelbroker, and the conditions page reserves throttling without naming a threshold.

identity_cost.detail: An account in the manager portal is required: the pricing block says 'Just created an account in our manager'. The sign-in page at manager.route64.org returned a login wall to the reader, so the exact fields a new account must supply were not readable. Email is the minimum such a portal implies and is not confirmed.

reliability_note: conditions: reject, cancel, throttle or nullroute at any time without warning; 200M best effort; flow-spec analysis; multiple accounts cause suspension of all.
confidence_note: A live request from a client endpoint through a WireGuard tunnel to a service on the routed /56 would raise this to measured. Two things were read (home page, conditions page) and neither was probed.

evidence.proved: free /56 over WireGuard, the protocol table, 'Pricing? No!', and the config-sample sentence
'Our service is designed to deliver up to 200M throughput often more.', 'We can throttle your bandwidth at any time.', and the no-warning cancellation clauses

notes: The routed /56 is IPv6 only, so the inbound address is public but reachable only by clients that have IPv6. The /56 is routed to the tunnel endpoint, so the endpoint is what a user must already own: this composes with a free VM, it is not a substitute for one. UDP is carried because the prefix is routed IP, not a port forward; that is inferred from 'Subnet is route to your tunnel endpoint', not from a UDP sentence.

extras.wg_detail: No downloadable .conf is published. The self-service portal is the registration and the generator: 'Our system also generated configuration samples for tunnel config based on your information.' WireGuard is one of six offered protocols ('Wireguard yes yes' in the IPv4 and IPv6 endpoint table).
extras.volume_stated: Traffic is not metered and it is possible to get more transit if 200M is not enough. (transit text) The IPv6 tunnelbroker page publishes no byte allowance at all; the conditions page says 'This is a free best effort service.'
extras.transit_note: Route64's routers carry the tunnel traffic to and from its upstreams and peers
